text: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Fever and cough for three days.\nHOSPITAL COURSE: Patient received fluids and acetaminophen. Chest radiograph showed no focal consolidation. Symptoms improved without oxygen.\nDISCHARGE PLAN: Continue oral fluids and acetaminophen as needed. Follow up with primary care in one week.
reference_summary: Short admission for a self-limited febrile respiratory illness; improved with supportive care and discharged with primary-care follow-up.

text: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Worsening ankle swelling.\nHOSPITAL COURSE: Diuresis was started with improvement in edema and breathing. Creatinine remained stable. No chest pain was reported.\nDISCHARGE PLAN: Continue prescribed diuretic, monitor daily weight, and return for worsening breathlessness.
reference_summary: Volume overload improved after diuresis; renal function remained stable and the patient was discharged with weight monitoring instructions.

text: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Abdominal pain and nausea.\nHOSPITAL COURSE: CT showed uncomplicated diverticulitis without abscess. Pain improved on oral medication and the patient tolerated diet.\nDISCHARGE PLAN: Complete the antibiotic course and return for fever, vomiting, or worsening pain.
reference_summary: Uncomplicated diverticulitis improved with oral treatment; complete antibiotics and return for worsening symptoms.
